_about: Prior model recommendations by TRL band and process complexity. These are informed starting points, not benchmark results: replace them with your own runs (`foames-bench recommend --results runs/<id>`). See docs/model-matrix.md for the reasoning and the assumptions.
knowledge_basis: Model families and licences as publicly known up to mid-2026. No benchmark run with real agents backs these cells yet; the first pilot should.

oss.label: Free / open weights
oss.meaning: Open-weight models run locally (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM) or on a university cluster, driven by an open harness such as OpenCode or Aider. No per-token cost; you pay in hardware and setup time.

baseline.label: Baseline (low-cost hosted)
baseline.meaning: Smaller or mid-sized commercial models: cheap per task, good at well-specified single-module changes.

frontier.label: Frontier
frontier.meaning: The most capable commercial models. Highest cost per run; strongest at ambiguous, multi-module and integration work.

trl_bands.1-3: Concept and research: a method from a paper, a notebook, a thesis prototype on synthetic or historical data. Wrong answers cost time, not product.
trl_bands.4-6: Validation in the lab or on a pilot line: real machine data, a FoaMES site, people start reading the numbers.
trl_bands.7-9: Qualified and in production: the numbers drive shifts, maintenance and ERP postings. Wrong answers cost product or money.

complexity.low: One module, one data source, discrete counts: a counter rule, an OEE window, a report.
complexity.medium: Several modules or a statistical method: shift calendars with OEE, SPC rules, process mining over an event log, batch steps.
complexity.high: Several systems or regulated traceability: ERP postings, retries and idempotency, designation changes between batch and discrete, an ambiguous requirement that must be turned into a specification.

low.why: Well-specified, cheap to retry, and students learn more from reading the diff. A local 20-30B model is usually enough.

medium.why: Statistics and process mining reward care more than size; run two repetitions and keep the better-reasoned one. Escalate to baseline if the OSS model fails the invariant group.

high.why: Ambiguity is the hard part. Use a baseline model for the specification and a frontier model to critique it; OSS models tend to skip the 'what cannot be inferred' section.

low.why: Real plant data now; a cheap hosted model gives a reliable first attempt. A local model is fine if it passes both qualifying tasks on two repetitions.

medium.human_review: Code review and a check against plant data
medium.why: Multi-module work with statistics; baseline models usually pass, frontier models pass more often on the first try.

high.human_review: Design review with the process owner
high.why: Integration and idempotency mistakes duplicate ERP postings; the first-attempt rate matters more than the per-run price.

low.why: Simple changes, but in production. Require the agent's own tests to pass and every repetition to succeed.

medium.human_review: Two-person review, validation on historical data
medium.why: Production statistics feed decisions; pay for the higher first-attempt rate and keep a baseline model as a second opinion.

high.human_review: Formal change control; the agent proposes, people approve
high.why: Production ERP postings and regulated traceability. Use the strongest model you can, require reproducible success, and keep FoaMES's rule that agents suggest and people act. Open-weight models are fine for drafting tests only.
